title: DOW-UAP-PR085, "16 Sept 2020 [CALLSIGN] [CALLSIGN] observes UAP"
what_is_it: A military full-motion video recording from a sensor aboard a U.S. military platform, showing an unidentified aerial phenomenon observed in the CENTCOM area of responsibility.
core_summary: This is a 4-minute 44-second video recorded by a U.S. military platform operating in the CENTCOM area of responsibility in September 2020. The video shows a sensor tracking an area of contrast that enters the frame and is tracked as the camera pans, zooms, and attempts to hold the object in the center of the frame. The video was uploaded to a classified network in September 2020 and was later identified by AARO as part of a collection of potentially UAP-related records requested by eight members of the U.S. House of Representatives.
interpretation_warnings: No extracted text is available from the video itself; all facts are derived from metadata and the CSV description provided by war.gov.
AARO uses the word 'likely' when attributing the video to a U.S. military platform, indicating assessment rather than confirmed provenance.
The materials lack a substantiated chain-of-custody, meaning the video's origin and handling cannot be fully verified.
Callsigns in the title are redacted, preventing identification of the specific unit or platform involved.
The video description is truncated at 02:25-04:29, so the full content of the latter half of the video is not described in available metadata.
The title characterises the object as a 'UAP' but this is the uploader's description, not a formal classification by AARO or DOW.

public_headline: Military Video Shows Unidentified Object Tracked Over CENTCOM Region
public_tldr: This is a 4-minute 44-second video recorded by a U.S. military sensor platform in the Central Command (CENTCOM) area of responsibility on 16 September 2020, showing a tracked unidentified aerial phenomenon. The video was released after eight members of the U.S. House of Representatives requested access to 51 potentially UAP-related records in March 2026.
public_narrative:
On 16 September 2020, a U.S. military platform operating in the CENTCOM area of responsibility — a region covering the Middle East and parts of Central and South Asia — recorded a video of an unidentified aerial phenomenon using a full-motion video sensor. The recording runs 4 minutes and 44 seconds. The first 1 minute and 17 seconds contain no content. At the 1:18 mark, an area of contrast enters the bottom of the frame. The sensor pans, zooms, and attempts to hold the object in the centre of the frame as it moves.

The video was uploaded to a classified network in September 2020. It was later identified by the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) as part of a collection of potentially UAP-related materials. On 6 March 2026, eight members of the U.S. House of Representatives formally requested access to 51 such records, and this video was among the responsive materials AARO located.

The Department of War describes this as a video "likely" derived from a U.S. military platform — notably using the word "likely" rather than confirming the source outright. The callsigns in the document title are redacted, so the specific military unit or aircraft involved is not publicly identified.

Neither AARO nor the Department of War has offered a formal identification or explanation of what the object in the video is. The title's use of "UAP" reflects the uploader's description, not an official classification. The department also notes that many of the materials in this collection lack a substantiated chain of custody, meaning the full history of how this video was recorded, handled, and stored cannot be independently verified.
public_caveats: The Department of War says the video was 'likely' recorded by a U.S. military platform — this is an assessment, not confirmed provenance.
The materials lack a substantiated chain of custody, meaning the video's origin and handling history cannot be fully verified.
Callsigns in the title are redacted, so the specific unit, aircraft, or crew involved cannot be identified from public information.
Available metadata only describes the video up to the 2:25 mark; the content from 2:25 to 4:44 is not described, so roughly half the video's content is uncharacterised in official descriptions.
The label 'UAP' comes from the person who uploaded the video, not from a formal assessment by AARO or the Department of War.
